lede: Know where to ride, stay, eat and refill in Kamnik.
intro: Kamnik is an old town at the foot of the Kamnik and Savinja Alps, where the Kamniška Bistrica leaves the mountains for the plain north of Ljubljana. Ride north and the valley climbs towards the Velika planina cable car; ride south and the land opens out. The Prekmurje and Štajerska branch of the Jakobova pot, G7 and G13 meet here. L-041 runs from Mekinje to Kamniška Bistrica, following the valley into the mountains. Stahovica, Mekinje and the Tuhinj valley belong to Kamnik too.

routes.title: Cycle routes through Kamnik
routes.body: Four signed routes pass through Kamnik. The Jakobova pot covers 32 km here on its 263 km way across Slovenia. L-041, from Mekinje to Kamniška Bistrica, is a 12 km regional route up the valley, all of it in Kamnik. G7 from Kranj runs 4 km through town. G13, which runs from Ljubljana through Kamnik and Vransko to Celje, has 3 km here. For a longer day, Kamničanka takes you 72 km, an easy ride with 254 m of climbing.

stays.title: Where to stay with your bike
stays.body: Kamnik has 9 places to stay, and several are in the valley north of town. Pri planinskem orlu in Stahovica is a family inn with rooms, 40 metres from L-041. Further up, Kraljev hrib has a campsite 170 metres from the route and 300 metres from the Velika planina cable car. Kamp Resnik is 90 metres from the Jakobova pot and open from 1 May to 30 September. For a rest day, Terme Snovik in the Tuhinj valley is a thermal spa 920 metres from the same route.

food.title: Where to stop and eat
food.body: Kamnik has 13 places to eat. Picerija Murka, on the north side of town with a view of the mountains, is 20 metres from L-041 and bakes in a bread oven. In town, Picerija Napoli is 60 metres from G7 and open Monday to Saturday from 11:00 to 22:00, Sundays and holidays from 12:00 to 21:00. Up the valley, Kraljev hrib serves home cooking 160 metres from L-041. For Balkan food grilled over charcoal, Leskovački žar Kordun is on the Kamnik bypass, 1.0 km from G7.

practical.title: Water, repair and charging
practical.body: Kamnik has 26 public water points, but only 6 are within 150 metres of a signed route. There is one public repair stand and two bike shops, Bikes and Fun and Pro kolo. Kamnik has 5 public chargers, handy on an e-bike before the climb up the valley.

sights.title: What to see on the way
sights.body: The old town is full of stops, and most sit right on G7. Rudolf Maister's birth house is 10 metres from the route and the Little Castle 50 metres. Zaprice Mansion, 160 metres from G7, is now a museum. Up the valley, the Ursuline monastery at Mekinje is 80 metres from L-041, and the Upper Castle is 260 metres from the Jakobova pot.
